finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL. The only validation is host.endswith('example.com'), with no leading dot, so an attacker-registered domain such as evilexample.com or attacker-example.com passes. The hostname can also resolve to internal or metadata IPs. The defined ALLOWED_SUFFIX ('.example.com') is never used. There is no scheme restriction and no IP or DNS-rebinding check.

trace.note: url taken from the query string
weak check: host.endswith('example.com') without a dot boundary
request issued to the full attacker-controlled URL

finding.guards_checked: Suffix check at line 13 is bypassable (evilexample.com, or an attacker domain resolving to 169.254.169.254 or 127.0.0.1). ALLOWED_SUFFIX is unused. No scheme allowlist, no resolved-IP blocklist. httpx does not follow redirects by default, which limits redirect-based bypass, but direct requests to an attacker-owned matching domain are still possible. The /ping endpoint uses a hardcoded URL and is not vulnerable.

verdict.guard_found: none (only host.endswith('example.com') at mirror.py:13, a suffix check without a dot boundary; ALLOWED_SUFFIX at line 7 is unused; no auth or middleware in the only file)
verdict.reason: The `url` query param (mirror.py:11) is attacker-controlled and reaches c.get(url) at mirror.py:16 guarded only by the bypassable suffix check at mirror.py:13, so hosts like evilexample.com pass.
